paper_title: Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs
caption: Inter-annotator agreement compared to sample-level ambiguity standard deviation and sample-level maximum ambiguity values.
model_annotation: This figure consists of two side-by-side bar charts illustrating inter-annotator agreement, measured by Fleiss Kappa, in relation to sample-level ambiguity metrics. The left chart has a horizontal axis labeled "Ambiguity Std" with four categories: 0.0, 0.47, 0.82, and 0.94, ordered from left to right in ascending numerical order, and a vertical axis labeled "Fleiss Kappa" with a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to approximately 0.9, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. All bars are rendered in a dark teal-blue color. The bar at Ambiguity Std 0.0 is the tallest, reaching a value of 0.88 as annotated above it, followed by the bar at 0.47 with a value of 0.46, then the bar at 0.94 with a value of 0.24, and the shortest bar at 0.82 with a value of 0.03. The right chart has a horizontal axis labeled "Max Ambiguity" with three categories: 1, 2, and 3, ordered from left to right, and a vertical axis also labeled "Fleiss Kappa" with the same linear scale ranging from 0.0 to approximately 0.9 with tick marks at 0.2 intervals. The bars are the same dark teal-blue color. The tallest bar corresponds to Max Ambiguity value 1 with a Fleiss Kappa of 0.89, followed by the bar at Max Ambiguity 2 with a value of 0.46, and the shortest bar at Max Ambiguity 3 with a value of 0.23. Each bar in both charts is annotated with its exact numerical value displayed above the bar. The bars in both charts are not explicitly sorted by height but rather follow the ascending order of their respective horizontal axis categories, and no bars appear to be visually emphasized through shading, bolding, or outlining beyond the consistent coloring used throughout.
